package_info.why_malicious: These versions of xz-utils contain a supply chain backdoor (CVE-2024-3094) that enables remote, unauthenticated interference with SSHD authentication, potentially allowing attackers to gain unauthorized system access. The malicious code is injected via a manipulated M4 macro in the tarball source distribution, which triggers the build of a second-stage backdoor artifact.

execution_context.file_location: m4 macro file in tarball source distribution

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: A malicious M4 macro is included in the tarball, which, during the build process, triggers the compilation and inclusion of a backdoor into the resulting xz-utils binaries.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At build-time, the code injects a backdoor into the xz-utils binaries by conditionally compiling additional code if the malicious M4 macro is present, resulting in a compromised library.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The presence of undocumented and obfuscated build macros that alter the resulting binary is highly suspicious, especially when not present in the official Git repository.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal build macros should not introduce hidden functionality or alter authentication mechanisms. Here, the macro introduces a backdoor without user knowledge.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: M4 macros are legitimately used to configure builds, but not to inject hidden authentication bypasses.
key_indicators: Obfuscated or undocumented M4 macro in source tarball
Macro triggers compilation of hidden code not present in main source

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when SSHD uses liblzma from xz-utils)
required_permissions: potentially network if exfiltration is attempted

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Injected code in the compiled liblzma library hooks into SSHD authentication routines, allowing remote, unauthenticated interference with SSHD authentication.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when SSHD loads the compromised liblzma, the injected code intercepts authentication routines, enabling an attacker to bypass normal authentication and gain unauthorized access.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Library code should not interfere with authentication mechanisms of unrelated services. The code is designed to subvert SSHD authentication, which is a critical security violation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Compression libraries are not expected to interact with or alter authentication logic in SSHD.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None. Compression libraries should not affect authentication.
key_indicators: Library code hooks into SSHD authentication
Behavior only present in binaries built from tarball, not from Git

attack_chain.action: Malicious M4 macro in tarball triggers injection of backdoor code during build process.
Compromised xz-utils library is installed on target system and loaded by SSHD.
attack_chain.leads_to: Runtime execution of injected backdoor code.

attack_chain.action: Injected code in liblzma intercepts SSHD authentication, enabling remote, unauthenticated access.

behavioral_signatures: Presence of undocumented or obfuscated M4 macros in build scripts
xz-utils binaries with unexpected code paths or authentication hooks
liblzma library interfering with SSHD authentication
file_indicators: M4 macro files in tarball source not present in official Git repository
xz-utils binaries (liblzma) with altered hashes compared to official builds
network_indicators: Unusual SSHD authentication attempts succeeding without valid credentials
Potential outbound connections if exfiltration is attempted (not confirmed in this report)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Compare xz-utils tarball source and build artifacts against official Git repository and known-good binaries. Look for undocumented M4 macros and differences in build scripts. Monitor SSHD logs for unexpected authentication successes. Use file integrity monitoring to detect altered liblzma binaries. Analyze binaries for unexpected code paths or hooks into authentication routines.
